writeup.headline: TIC Solutions rates Sell at 37: fast revenue growth, but heavy debt, thin cash flow and a weak trend.
writeup.thesis: TIC scores 37, a Sell with Medium confidence, sitting 8 points from both Hold and Strong Sell. Growth is the strongest factor (64), with quarterly revenue up 86.14% year over year, though growth slowed by 22.23 percentage points. The balance sheet scores just 11: net debt is 56.26 times free cash flow and cash covers only 0.22 of debt. Valuation scores 17. In absolute terms P/S of 0.922 is low, but P/FCF of 85.222 is high, and EV/EBIT cannot be calculated because EBIT is negative. There is no comparison with its own history. Quality (38) is held back by a -2.15% operating margin and a 1.08% FCF margin, the trend (28) is weak with the stock 34.83% below its 52-week high, and news is neutral at 50.
key_risks: High leverage: net debt is 56.26 times free cash flow, and cash covers only 0.22 of debt
Operating margin of -2.15% and FCF margin of 1.08% leave little cushion
Revenue growth is slowing, down 22.23 percentage points, and the August acquisitions add integration risk
Weak price trend: 12-1 momentum is -24.63% and the stock is 34.83% below its 52-week high
Confidence is limited because TTM revenue growth, dilution data and valuation history are missing
what_would_change: Up to Hold (8 points needed): stronger free cash flow that cuts net debt to FCF and lifts the balance sheet and valuation scores
Up: operating margin turning positive, which would improve quality and make EV/EBIT measurable
Down to Strong Sell (8-point drop): further slowing in growth, a worsening price trend, or negative guidance or other news at Q3 results
Confidence would change once TTM revenue, dilution data and 24 month-ends of valuation history become available
